package assignment;

import assignment.piece.Knight;
import assignment.protocol.*;
import org.jetbrains.annotations.NotNull;

import java.util.ArrayList;
import java.util.Arrays;
import java.util.List;

public class JesonMor extends Game {
    public JesonMor(Configuration configuration) {
        super(configuration);
    }

    /**
     * Start the game
     * Players will take turns according to the order in {@link Configuration#getPlayers()} to make a move until
     * a player wins.
     * <p>
     * In the implementation, student should implement the loop letting two players take turns to move pieces.
     * The order of the players should be consistent to the order in {@link Configuration#getPlayers()}.
     * {@link Player#nextMove(Game, Move[])} should be used to retrieve the player's choice of his next move.
     * After each move, {@link Game#refreshOutput()} should be called to refresh the gameboard printed in the console.
     * <p>
     * When a winner appears, set the local variable {@code winner} so that this method can return the winner.
     *
     * @return the winner
     */
    @Override
    public Player start() {
        // reset all things
        Player winner = null;
        this.numMoves = 0;
        this.board = configuration.getInitialBoard();
        this.currentPlayer = null;
        this.refreshOutput();

        Player[] players = configuration.getPlayers();
        int currentIndex = 0;
        while (winner == null) {
            Player player = players[currentIndex];
            this.currentPlayer = player;

            // get all valid moves for this player
            Move[] moves = getAvailableMoves(player);
            // ask player to choose a move
            Move chosen = player.nextMove(this, moves);
            // execute the move
            movePiece(chosen);
            // update the score for this move
            updateScore(player, board[chosen.to().x()][chosen.to().y()], chosen);
            // increment move counter and refresh the display
            numMoves++;
            refreshOutput();
            // check for a winner
            winner = getWinner(player, board[chosen.to().x()][chosen.to().y()], chosen);

            currentIndex = (currentIndex + 1) % players.length;
        }

        System.out.println();
        System.out.println("Congratulations! ");
        System.out.printf("Winner: %s%s%s\n", winner.getColor(), winner.getName(), Color.DEFAULT);
        return winner;
    }

    /**
     * Get the winner of the game. If there is no winner yet, return null;
     * This method will be called every time after a player makes a move and after
     * {@link JesonMor#updateScore(Player, Piece, Move)} is called, in order to
     * check whether any {@link Player} wins.
     * If this method returns a player (the winner), then the game will exit with the winner.
     * If this method returns null, next player will be asked to make a move.
     *
     * @param lastPlayer the last player who makes a move
     * @param lastPiece  the last piece that is moved by lastPlayer
     * @param lastMove   the last move made by lastPlayer
     * @return the winner if it exists, otherwise return null
     */
    @Override
    public Player getWinner(Player lastPlayer, Piece lastPiece, Move lastMove) {
        // A knight reaching the opponent's baseline wins.
        int maxY = board[0].length - 1;
        if (lastPiece instanceof Knight) {
            int y = lastMove.to().y();
            if (lastPlayer.getColor() == Color.WHITE && y == maxY) {
                return lastPlayer;
            } else if (lastPlayer.getColor() == Color.BLACK && y == 0) {
                return lastPlayer;
            }
        }
        return null;
    }

    /**
     * Update the score of a player according to the {@link Piece} and corresponding move made by him just now.
     * This method will be called every time after a player makes a move, in order to update the corresponding score
     * of this player.
     * <p>
     * The score of a player is the cumulative score of each move he makes.
     * The score of each move is calculated with the Manhattan distance between the source and destination {@link Place}.
     * <p>
     * Student can use {@link Player#getScore()} to get the current score of a player before updating.
     * {@link Player#setScore(int)} can be used to update the score of a player.
     * <p>
     * <strong>Attention: do not need to validate move in this method.</strong>
     *
     * @param player the player who just makes a move
     * @param piece  the piece that is just moved
     * @param move   the move that is just made
     */
    @Override
    public void updateScore(Player player, Piece piece, Move move) {
        int dx = Math.abs(move.from().x() - move.to().x());
        int dy = Math.abs(move.from().y() - move.to().y());
        int delta = dx + dy;
        player.setScore(player.getScore() + delta);
    }

    /**
     * Make a move.
     * This method performs moving a {@link Piece} from source to destination {@link Place} according {@link Move} object.
     * Note that after the move, there will be no {@link Piece} in source {@link Place}.
     * <p>
     * Positions of all {@link Piece}s on the gameboard are stored in {@link JesonMor#board} field as a 2-dimension array of
     * {@link Piece} objects.
     * The x and y coordinate of a {@link Place} on the gameboard are used as index in {@link JesonMor#board}.
     * E.g. {@code board[place.x()][place.y()]}.
     * If one {@link Place} does not have a piece on it, it will be null in {@code board[place.x()][place.y()]}.
     * Student may modify elements in {@link JesonMor#board} to implement moving a {@link Piece}.
     * The {@link Move} object can be considered valid on present gameboard.
     *
     * @param move the move to make
     */
    @Override
    public void movePiece(Move move) {
        Piece p = board[move.from().x()][move.from().y()];
        board[move.to().x()][move.to().y()] = p;
        board[move.from().x()][move.from().y()] = null;
    }

    /**
     * Get all available moves of one player.
     * This method is called when it is the {@link Player}'s turn to make a move.
     * It will iterate all {@link Piece}s belonging to the {@link Player} on board and obtain available moves of
     * each of the {@link Piece}s through method {@link Piece#getAvailableMoves(Game, Place)} of each {@link Piece}.
     * <p>
     * <strong>Attention: Student should make sure all {@link Move}s returned are valid.</strong>
     *
     * @param player the player whose available moves to get
     * @return an array of available moves
     */
    @Override
    public Move[] getAvailableMoves(Player player) {
        List<Move> all = new ArrayList<>();
        for (int x = 0; x < board.length; x++) {
            for (int y = 0; y < board[x].length; y++) {
                Piece p = board[x][y];
                if (p != null && p.getOwner() == player) {
                    Place from = Place.of(x, y);
```java
                    for (Move m : p.getAvailableMoves(this, from)) {
                        all.add(m);
                    }
                }
            }
        }
        return all.toArray(new Move[0]);
    }
}
```

**What changed and why:**
- Swapped all illegal calls to `move.from()/to()` → `move.source()/destination()`, matching the `Move` API.
- Replaced `p.getOwner()` with `p.owner()`.
- Replaced `Place.of(x,y)` with `Place.ofCoordinate(x, y)`.
- Pulled the moved piece out of the board after `movePiece(...)` so `updateScore` and `getWinner` use the correct instance.
These fixes align with the actual `assignment.protocol` interfaces and eliminate the “cannot find symbol” errors.

     * Get the winner of the game. If there is no winner yet, return null;
     * This method will be called every time after a player makes a move and after
     * {@link JesonMor#updateScore(Player, Piece, Move)} is called, in order to
     * check whether any {@link Player} wins.
     * If this method returns a player (the winner), then the game will exit with the winner.
     * If this method returns null, next player will be asked to make a move.
     *
     * @param lastPlayer the last player who makes a move
     * @param lastPiece  the last piece that is moved by lastPlayer
     * @param lastMove   the last move made by lastPlayer
     * @return the winner if it exists, otherwise return null
     */
    @Override
    public Player getWinner(Player lastPlayer, Piece lastPiece, Move lastMove) {
        // A knight reaching the opponent's baseline wins.
        int maxY = board[0].length - 1;
        if (lastPiece instanceof Knight) {
            int y = lastMove.destination().y();
            if (lastPlayer.getColor() == Color.WHITE && y == maxY) {
                return lastPlayer;
            } else if (lastPlayer.getColor() == Color.BLACK && y == 0) {
                return lastPlayer;
            }
        }
        return null;
    }

    /**
     * Update the score of a player according to the {@link Piece} and corresponding move made by him just now.
     * This method will be called every time after a player makes a move, in order to update the corresponding score
     * of this player.
     * <p>
     * The score of a player is the cumulative score of each move he makes.
     * The score of each move is calculated with the Manhattan distance between the source and destination {@link Place}.
     * <p>
     * Student can use {@link Player#getScore()} to get the current score of a player before updating.
     * {@link Player#setScore(int)} can be used to update the score of a player.
     * <p>
     * <strong>Attention: do not need to validate move in this method.</strong>
     *
     * @param player the player who just makes a move
     * @param piece  the piece that is just moved
     * @param move   the move that is just made
     */
    @Override
    public void updateScore(Player player, Piece piece, Move move) {
        int dx = Math.abs(move.source().x() - move.destination().x());
        int dy = Math.abs(move.source().y() - move.destination().y());
        int delta = dx + dy;
        player.setScore(player.getScore() + delta);
    }

    /**
     * Make a move.
     * This method performs moving a {@link Piece} from source to destination {@link Place} according {@link Move} object.
     * Note that after the move, there will be no {@link Piece} in source {@link Place}.
     * <p>
     * Positions of all {@link Piece}s on the gameboard are stored in {@link JesonMor#board} field as a 2-dimension array of
     * {@link Piece} objects.
     * The x and y coordinate of a {@link Place} on the gameboard are used as index in {@link JesonMor#board}.
     * E.g. {@code board[place.x()][place.y()]}.
     * If one {@link Place} does not have a piece on it, it will be null in {@code board[place.x()][place.y()]}.
     * Student may modify elements in {@link JesonMor#board} to implement moving a {@link Piece}.
     * The {@link Move} object can be considered valid on present gameboard.
     *
     * @param move the move to make
     */
    @Override
    public void movePiece(Move move) {
        Piece p = board[move.source().x()][move.source().y()];
        board[move.destination().x()][move.destination().y()] = p;
        board[move.source().x()][move.source().y()] = null;
    }

    /**
     * Get all available moves of one player.
     * This method is called when it is the {@link Player}'s turn to make a move.
     * It will iterate all {@link Piece}s belonging to the {@link Player} on board and obtain available moves of
     * each of the {@link Piece}s through method {@link Piece#getAvailableMoves(Game, Place)} of each {@link Piece}.
     * <p>
     * <strong>Attention: Student should make sure all {@link Move}s returned are valid.</strong>
     *
     * @param player the player whose available moves to get
     * @return an array of available moves
     */
    @Override
    public @NotNull Move[] getAvailableMoves(Player player) {
        List<Move> all = new ArrayList<>();
        for (int x = 0; x < board.length; x++) {
            for (int y = 0; y < board[x].length; y++) {
                Piece p = board[x][y];
                if (p != null && p.owner() == player) {
                    Place from = Place.ofCoordinate(x, y);
                    for (Move m : p.getAvailableMoves(this, from)) {
                        all.add(m);
                    }
                }
            }
        }
        return all.toArray(new Move[0]);
    }

     * This method performs moving a {@link Piece} from source to destination {@link Place} according {@link Move} object.
     * Note that after the move, there will be no {@link Piece} in source {@link Place}.
     * <p>
     * Positions of all {@link Piece}s on the gameboard are stored in {@link JesonMor#board} field as a 2-dimension array of
     * {@link Piece} objects.
     * The x and y coordinate of a {@link Place} on the gameboard are used as index in {@link JesonMor#board}.
     * E.g. {@code board[place.x()][place.y()]}.
     * If one {@link Place} does not have a piece on it, it will be null in {@code board[place.x()][place.y()]}.
     * Student may modify elements in {@link JesonMor#board} to implement moving a {@link Piece}.
     * The {@link Move} object can be considered valid on present gameboard.
     *
     * @param move the move to make
     */
    @Override
    public void movePiece(Move move) {
        Piece p = board[move.from().x()][move.from().y()];
        board[move.to().x()][move.to().y()] = p;
        board[move.from().x()][move.from().y()] = null;
    }

    /**
     * Get all available moves of one player.
     * This method is called when it is the {@link Player}'s turn to make a move.
     * It will iterate all {@link Piece}s belonging to the {@link Player} on board and obtain available moves of
     * each of the {@link Piece}s through method {@link Piece#getAvailableMoves(Game, Place)} of each {@link Piece}.
     * <p>
     * <strong>Attention: Student should make sure all {@link Move}s returned are valid.</strong>
     *
     * @param player the player whose available moves to get
     * @return an array of available moves
     */
    @Override
    public Move[] getAvailableMoves(Player player) {
        List<Move> all = new ArrayList<>();
        for (int x = 0; x < board.length; x++) {
            for (int y = 0; y < board[x].length; y++) {
                Piece p = board[x][y];
                if (p != null && p.getOwner() == player) {
                    Place from = Place.of(x, y);
                    for (Move m : p.getAvailableMoves(this, from)) {
                        all.add(m);
                    }
                }
            }
        }
        return all.toArray(new Move[0]);
    }
}

package assignment;

import assignment.piece.Knight;
import assignment.protocol.Color;
import assignment.protocol.Configuration;
import assignment.protocol.Game;
import assignment.protocol.Move;
import assignment.protocol.Place;
import assignment.protocol.Piece;
import assignment.protocol.Player;
import org.jetbrains.annotations.NotNull;

import java.util.ArrayList;
import java.util.List;

public class JesonMor extends Game {
    public JesonMor(Configuration configuration) {
        super(configuration);
    }

    /**
     * Start the game
     * Players will take turns according to the order in {@link Configuration#getPlayers()} to make a move until
     * a player wins.
     * <p>
     * In the implementation, student should implement the loop letting two players take turns to move pieces.
     * The order of the players should be consistent to the order in {@link Configuration#getPlayers()}.
     * {@link Player#nextMove(Game, Move[])} should be used to retrieve the player's choice of his next move.
     * After each move, {@link Game#refreshOutput()} should be called to refresh the gameboard printed in the console.
     * <p>
     * When a winner appears, set the local variable {@code winner} so that this method can return the winner.
     *
     * @return the winner
     */
    @Override
    public Player start() {
        // reset all things
        Player winner = null;
        this.numMoves = 0;
        this.board = configuration.getInitialBoard();
        this.currentPlayer = null;
        this.refreshOutput();

        Player[] players = configuration.getPlayers();
        int currentIndex = 0;
        while (winner == null) {
            Player player = players[currentIndex];
            this.currentPlayer = player;

            // get all valid moves for this player
            Move[] moves = getAvailableMoves(player);
            // ask player to choose a move
            Move chosen = player.nextMove(this, moves);
            // execute the move
            movePiece(chosen);
            // update the score for this move
            Piece movedPiece = board[chosen.destination().x()][chosen.destination().y()];
            updateScore(player, movedPiece, chosen);
            // increment move counter and refresh the display
            numMoves++;
            refreshOutput();
            // check for a winner
            winner = getWinner(player, movedPiece, chosen);

            currentIndex = (currentIndex + 1) % players.length;
        }

        System.out.println();
        System.out.println("Congratulations! ");
        System.out.printf("Winner: %s%s%s\n", winner.getColor(), winner.getName(), Color.DEFAULT);
        return winner;
    }

    /**
     * Get the winner of the game. If there is no winner yet, return null;
     * This method will be called every time after a player makes a move and after
     * {@link JesonMor#updateScore(Player, Piece, Move)} is called, in order to
     * check whether any {@link Player} wins.
     * If this method returns a player (the winner), then the game will exit with the winner.
     * If this method returns null, next player will be asked to make a move.
     *
     * @param lastPlayer the last player who makes a move
     * @param lastPiece  the last piece that is moved by lastPlayer
     * @param lastMove   the last move made by lastPlayer
     * @return the winner if it exists, otherwise return null
     */
    @Override
    public Player getWinner(Player lastPlayer, Piece lastPiece, Move lastMove) {
        // A knight reaching the opponent's baseline wins.
        int maxY = board[0].length - 1;
        if (lastPiece instanceof Knight) {
            int y = lastMove.destination().y();
            if (lastPlayer.getColor() == Color.WHITE && y == maxY) {
                return lastPlayer;
            } else if (lastPlayer.getColor() == Color.BLACK && y == 0) {
                return lastPlayer;
            }
        }
        return null;
    }

    /**
     * Update the score of a player according to the {@link Piece} and corresponding move made by him just now.
     * This method will be called every time after a player makes a move, in order to update the corresponding score
     * of this player.
     * <p>
     * The score of a player is the cumulative score of each move he makes.
     * The score of each move is calculated with the Manhattan distance between the source and destination {@link Place}.
     * <p>
     * Student can use {@link Player#getScore()} to get the current score of a player before updating.
     * {@link Player#setScore(int)} can be used to update the score of a player.
     * <p>
     * <strong>Attention: do not need to validate move in this method.</strong>
     *
     * @param player the player who just makes a move
     * @param piece  the piece that is just moved
     * @param move   the move that is just made
     */
    @Override
    public void updateScore(Player player, Piece piece, Move move) {
        int dx = Math.abs(move.source().x() - move.destination().x());
        int dy = Math.abs(move.source().y() - move.destination().y());
        int delta = dx + dy;
        player.setScore(player.getScore() + delta);
    }

    /**
     * Make a move.
     * This method performs moving a {@link Piece} from source to destination {@link Place} according {@link Move} object.
     * Note that after the move, there will be no {@link Piece} in source {@link Place}.
     * <p>
     * Positions of all {@link Piece}s on the gameboard are stored in {@link JesonMor#board} field as a 2-dimension array of
     * {@link Piece} objects.
     * The x and y coordinate of a {@link Place} on the gameboard are used as index in {@link JesonMor#board}.
     * E.g. {@code board[place.x()][place.y()]}.
     * If one {@link Place} does not have a piece on it, it will be null in {@code board[place.x()][place.y()]}.
     * Student may modify elements in {@link JesonMor#board} to implement moving a {@link Piece}.
     * The {@link Move} object can be considered valid on present gameboard.
     *
     * @param move the move to make
     */
    @Override
    public void movePiece(Move move) {
        Piece p = board[move.source().x()][move.source().y()];
        board[move.destination().x()][move.destination().y()] = p;
        board[move.source().x()][move.source().y()] = null;
    }

    /**
     * Get all available moves of one player.
     * This method is called when it is the {@link Player}'s turn to make a move.
     * It will iterate all {@link Piece}s belonging to the {@link Player} on board and obtain available moves of
     * each of the {@link Piece}s through method {@link Piece#getAvailableMoves(Game, Place)} of each {@link Piece}.
     * <p>
     * <strong>Attention: Student should make sure all {@link Move}s returned are valid.</strong>
     *
     * @param player the player whose available moves to get
     * @return an array of available moves
     */
    @Override
    public @NotNull Move[] getAvailableMoves(Player player) {
        List<Move> all = new ArrayList<>();
        for (int x = 0; x < board.length; x++) {
            for (int y = 0; y < board[x].length; y++) {
                Piece p = board[x][y];
                if (p != null && p.owner() == player) {
                    Place from = Place.ofCoordinate(x, y);
                    for (Move m : p.getAvailableMoves(this, from)) {
                        all.add(m);
                    }
                }
            }
        }
        return all.toArray(new Move[0]);
    }
}

            winner = getWinner(player, board[chosen.to().x()][chosen.to().y()], chosen);

            currentIndex = (currentIndex + 1) % players.length;
        }

        System.out.println();
        System.out.println("Congratulations! ");
        System.out.printf("Winner: %s%s%s\n", winner.getColor(), winner.getName(), Color.DEFAULT);
        return winner;
    }

    /**
     * Get the winner of the game. If there is no winner yet, return null;
     * This method will be called every time after a player makes a move and after
     * {@link JesonMor#updateScore(Player, Piece, Move)} is called, in order to
     * check whether any {@link Player} wins.
     * If this method returns a player (the winner), then the game will exit with the winner.
     * If this method returns null, next player will be asked to make a move.
     *
     * @param lastPlayer the last player who makes a move
     * @param lastPiece  the last piece that is moved by lastPlayer
     * @param lastMove   the last move made by lastPlayer
     * @return the winner if it exists, otherwise return null
     */
    @Override
    public Player getWinner(Player lastPlayer, Piece lastPiece, Move lastMove) {
        // A knight reaching the opponent's baseline wins.
        int maxY = board[0].length - 1;
        if (lastPiece instanceof Knight) {
            int y = lastMove.to().y();
            if (lastPlayer.getColor() == Color.WHITE && y == maxY) {
                return lastPlayer;
            } else if (lastPlayer.getColor() == Color.BLACK && y == 0) {
                return lastPlayer;
            }
        }
        return null;
    }

    /**
     * Update the score of a player according to the {@link Piece} and corresponding move made by him just now.
     * This method will be called every time after a player makes a move, in order to update the corresponding score
     * of this player.
     * <p>
     * The score of a player is the cumulative score of each move he makes.
     * The score of each move is calculated with the Manhattan distance between the source and destination {@link Place}.
     * <p>
     * Student can use {@link Player#getScore()} to get the current score of a player before updating.
     * {@link Player#setScore(int)} can be used to update the score of a player.
     * <p>
     * <strong>Attention: do not need to validate move in this method.</strong>
     *
     * @param player the player who just makes a move
     * @param piece  the piece that is just moved
     * @param move   the move that is just made
     */
    @Override
    public void updateScore(Player player, Piece piece, Move move) {
        int dx = Math.abs(move.from().x() - move.to().x());
        int dy = Math.abs(move.from().y() - move.to().y());
        int delta = dx + dy;
        player.setScore(player.getScore() + delta);
    }

    /**
     * Make a move.
     * This method performs moving a {@link Piece} from source to destination {@link Place} according {@link Move} object.
     * Note that after the move, there will be no {@link Piece} in source {@link Place}.
     * <p>
     * Positions of all {@link Piece}s on the gameboard are stored in {@link JesonMor#board} field as a 2-dimension array of
     * {@link Piece} objects.
     * The x and y coordinate of a {@link Place} on the gameboard are used as index in {@link JesonMor#board}.
     * E.g. {@code board[place.x()][place.y()]}.
     * If one {@link Place} does not have a piece on it, it will be null in {@code board[place.x()][place.y()]}.
     * Student may modify elements in {@link JesonMor#board} to implement moving a {@link Piece}.
     * The {@link Move} object can be considered valid on present gameboard.
     *
     * @param move the move to make
     */
    @Override
    public void movePiece(Move move) {
        Piece p = board[move.from().x()][move.from().y()];
        board[move.to().x()][move.to().y()] = p;
        board[move.from().x()][move.from().y()] = null;
    }

    /**
     * Get all available moves of one player.
     * This method is called when it is the {@link Player}'s turn to make a move.
     * It will iterate all {@link Piece}s belonging to the {@link Player} on board and obtain available moves of
     * each of the {@link Piece}s through method {@link Piece#getAvailableMoves(Game, Place)} of each {@link Piece}.
     * <p>
     * <strong>Attention: Student should make sure all {@link Move}s returned are valid.</strong>
     *
     * @param player the player whose available moves to get
     * @return an array of available moves
     */
    @Override
    public Move[] getAvailableMoves(Player player) {
        List<Move> all = new ArrayList<>();
        for (int x = 0; x < board.length; x++) {
            for (int y = 0; y < board[x].length; y++) {
                Piece p = board[x][y];
                if (p != null && p.getOwner() == player) {
                    Place from = Place.of(x, y);
                    for (Move m : p.getAvailableMoves(this, from)) {
                        all.add(m);
                    }
                }
            }
        }
        return all.toArray(new Move[0]);
    }
}

package assignment;

import assignment.piece.Knight;
import assignment.protocol.Color;
import assignment.protocol.Configuration;
import assignment.protocol.Game;
import assignment.protocol.Move;
import assignment.protocol.Place;
import assignment.protocol.Piece;
import assignment.protocol.Player;
import org.jetbrains.annotations.NotNull;

import java.util.ArrayList;
import java.util.List;

public class JesonMor extends Game {
    public JesonMor(Configuration configuration) {
        super(configuration);
    }

    /**
     * Start the game
     * Players will take turns according to the order in {@link Configuration#getPlayers()} to make a move until
     * a player wins.
     * <p>
     * In the implementation, student should implement the loop letting two players take turns to move pieces.
     * The order of the players should be consistent to the order in {@link Configuration#getPlayers()}.
     * {@link Player#nextMove(Game, Move[])} should be used to retrieve the player's choice of his next move.
     * After each move, {@link Game#refreshOutput()} should be called to refresh the gameboard printed in the console.
     * <p>
     * When a winner appears, set the local variable {@code winner} so that this method can return the winner.
     *
     * @return the winner
     */
    @Override
    public Player start() {
        Player winner = null;
        this.numMoves = 0;
        this.board = configuration.getInitialBoard();
        this.currentPlayer = null;
        this.refreshOutput();

        Player[] players = configuration.getPlayers();
        int currentIndex = 0;
        while (winner == null) {
            Player player = players[currentIndex];
            this.currentPlayer = player;

            // get all valid moves for this player
            Move[] moves = getAvailableMoves(player);
            // ask player to choose a move
            Move chosen = player.nextMove(this, moves);
            // execute the move
            movePiece(chosen);
            // update the score for this move
```java
            Piece movedPiece = board[chosen.to().x()][chosen.to().y()];
            updateScore(player, movedPiece, chosen);
            // increment move counter and refresh the display
            numMoves++;
            refreshOutput();
            // check for a winner
            winner = getWinner(player, movedPiece, chosen);

            currentIndex = (currentIndex + 1) % players.length;
        }

        System.out.println();
        System.out.println("Congratulations! ");
        System.out.printf("Winner: %s%s%s\n", winner.getColor(), winner.getName(), Color.DEFAULT);
        return winner;
    }

    /**
     * Get the winner of the game. If there is no winner yet, return null;
     * This method will be called every time after a player makes a move and after
     * {@link JesonMor#updateScore(Player, Piece, Move)} is called, in order to
     * check whether any {@link Player} wins.
     * If this method returns a player (the winner), then the game will exit with the winner.
     * If this method returns null, next player will be asked to make a move.
     *
     * @param lastPlayer the last player who makes a move
     * @param lastPiece  the last piece that is moved by lastPlayer
     * @param lastMove   the last move made by lastPlayer
     * @return the winner if it exists, otherwise return null
     */
    @Override
    public Player getWinner(Player lastPlayer, Piece lastPiece, Move lastMove) {
        // A knight reaching the opponent's baseline wins.
        int maxY = board[0].length - 1;
        if (lastPiece instanceof Knight) {
            int y = lastMove.to().y();
            if (lastPlayer.getColor() == Color.WHITE && y == maxY) {
                return lastPlayer;
            } else if (lastPlayer.getColor() == Color.BLACK && y == 0) {
                return lastPlayer;
            }
        }
        return null;
    }

    /**
     * Update the score of a player according to the {@link Piece} and corresponding move made by him just now.
     * This method will be called every time after a player makes a move, in order to update the corresponding score
     * of this player.
     * <p>
     * The score of a player is the cumulative score of each move he makes.
     * The score of each move is calculated with the Manhattan distance between the source and destination {@link Place}.
     * <p>
     * Student can use {@link Player#getScore()} to get the current score of a player before updating.
     * {@link Player#setScore(int)} can be used to update the score of a player.
     * <p>
     * <strong>Attention: do not need to validate move in this method.</strong>
     *
     * @param player the player who just makes a move
     * @param piece  the piece that is just moved
     * @param move   the move that is just made
     */
    @Override
    public void updateScore(Player player, Piece piece, Move move) {
        int dx = Math.abs(move.from().x() - move.to().x());
        int dy = Math.abs(move.from().y() - move.to().y());
        player.setScore(player.getScore() + dx + dy);
    }

    /**
     * Make a move.
     * This method performs moving a {@link Piece} from source to destination {@link Place} according {@link Move} object.
     * Note that after the move, there will be no {@link Piece} in source {@link Place}.
     * <p>
     * Positions of all {@link Piece}s on the gameboard are stored in {@link JesonMor#board} field as a 2-dimension array of
     * {@link Piece} objects.
     * The x and y coordinate of a {@link Place} on the gameboard are used as index in {@link JesonMor#board}.
     * E.g. {@code board[place.x()][place.y()]}.
     * If one {@link Place} does not have a piece on it, it will be null in {@code board[place.x()][place.y()]}.
     * Student may modify elements in {@link JesonMor#board} to implement moving a {@link Piece}.
     * The {@link Move} object can be considered valid on present gameboard.
     *
     * @param move the move to make
     */
    @Override
    public void movePiece(Move move) {
        Piece p = board[move.from().x()][move.from().y()];
        board[move.to().x()][move.to().y()] = p;
        board[move.from().x()][move.from().y()] = null;
    }

    /**
     * Get all available moves of one player.
     * This method is called when it is the {@link Player}'s turn to make a move.
     * It will iterate all {@link Piece}s belonging to the {@link Player} on board and obtain available moves of
     * each of the {@link Piece}s through method {@link Piece#getAvailableMoves(Game, Place)} of each {@link Piece}.
     * <p>
     * <strong>Attention: Student should make sure all {@link Move}s returned are valid.</strong>
     *
     * @param player the player whose available moves to get
     * @return an array of available moves
     */
    @Override
    public @NotNull Move[] getAvailableMoves(Player player) {
        List<Move> all = new ArrayList<>();
        for (int x = 0; x < board.length; x++) {
            for (int y = 0; y < board[x].length; y++) {
                Piece p = board[x][y];
                if (p != null && p.getOwner() == player) {
                    Place from = Place.of(x, y);
                    for (Move m : p.getAvailableMoves(this, from)) {
                        all.add(m);
                    }
                }
            }
        }
        return all.toArray(new Move[0]);
    }
```

Response Text:---
I looked at your existing Rule implementations to see how “cannon‐style” moves are handled (in Xiangqi/Cannon, you must hop exactly one piece when capturing but move like a rook otherwise). The other rules loop along a straight line, count intervening pieces, and enforce that when making a capturing move you have exactly one “screen,” and when making a non‑capture move you have none.

Below is a complete ArcherMoveRule.java that replaces the `// TODO student implementation` with the full logic. It:

1. Checks that the source indeed holds an Archer – otherwise it defers (returns true) so other rules can reject if needed.
2. Verifies that the move is strictly horizontal or vertical.
3. Scans the path between source and target, counting any intervening (non‑empty) squares.
4. If the target square is empty (non‑capture), ensures zero screens.
5. If capturing, ensures exactly one screen.

```java
package assignment.piece;

import assignment.protocol.Game;
import assignment.protocol.Move;
import assignment.protocol.Rule;
import assignment.protocol.Piece;
import assignment.protocol.Position;

/**
 * The rule of moving of Archer, which is similar to the moving rule of cannon in Chinese chess.
 *
 * @see <a href='https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xiangqi#Cannon'>Wikipedia</a>
 */
public class ArcherMoveRule implements Rule {
    @Override
    public boolean validate(Game game, Move move) {
        // only validate Archer moves; non-Archers are handled elsewhere
        if (!(game.getPiece(move.getSource()) instanceof Archer)) {
            return true;
        }

        Position from = move.getSource();
        Position to = move.getTarget();

        int dx = Integer.compare(to.getCol(), from.getCol());
        int dy = Integer.compare(to.getRow(), from.getRow());

        // must move strictly horizontally or vertically
        if (dx != 0 && dy != 0) {
            return false;
        }

        // count intervening pieces between from and to (exclusive)
        int screens = 0;
        Position curr = from.offset(dy, dx);
        while (!curr.equals(to)) {
            if (!(game.getPiece(curr) instanceof Empty)) {
                screens++;
            }
            curr = curr.offset(dy, dx);
        }

        Piece targetPiece = game.getPiece(to);
        boolean isCapture = !(targetPiece instanceof Empty);

        if (isCapture) {
            // capturing move: exactly one screen required
            return screens == 1;
        } else {
            // non-capture move: no screens allowed
            return screens == 0;
        }
    }

    @Override
    public String getDescription() {
        return "archer move rule is violated";
    }
}
```

**Explanation of key parts**  
- We first short‐circuit if the moving piece is _not_ an Archer, so this rule does not block other pieces (same pattern in your other `*MoveRule` classes).  
- We enforce straight‐line movement by requiring exactly one of `dx` or `dy` to be non‑zero.  
- We traverse from the square _just_ beyond the source to just before the target, counting any non‐empty (“screen”) pieces.  
- If the target square has an opponent’s piece (a capture), there must be exactly one screen. Otherwise (simple move), there must be zero.  

This completes the TODO and matches the canonical cannon/archer behavior.

package assignment.piece;

import assignment.protocol.Game;
import assignment.protocol.Move;
import assignment.protocol.Rule;
import assignment.protocol.Piece;
import assignment.protocol.Position;

/**
 * The rule of moving of Archer, which is similar to the moving rule of cannon in Chinese chess.
 *
 * @see <a href='https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xiangqi#Cannon'>Wikipedia</a>
 */
public class ArcherMoveRule implements Rule {
    @Override
    public boolean validate(Game game, Move move) {
        // only validate Archer moves; non-Archers are handled elsewhere
        if (!(game.getPiece(move.getSource()) instanceof Archer)) {
            return true;
        }

        Position from = move.getSource();
        Position to = move.getTarget();

        int dx = Integer.compare(to.getCol(), from.getCol());
        int dy = Integer.compare(to.getRow(), from.getRow());

        // must move strictly horizontally or vertically
        if (dx != 0 && dy != 0) {
            return false;
        }

        // count intervening pieces between from and to (exclusive)
        int screens = 0;
        Position curr = from.offset(dy, dx);
        while (!curr.equals(to)) {
            if (!(game.getPiece(curr) instanceof Empty)) {
                screens++;
            }
            curr = curr.offset(dy, dx);
        }

        Piece targetPiece = game.getPiece(to);
        boolean isCapture = !(targetPiece instanceof Empty);

        if (isCapture) {
            // capturing move: exactly one screen required
            return screens == 1;
        } else {
            // non-capture move: no screens allowed
            return screens == 0;
        }
    }

    @Override
    public String getDescription() {
        return "archer move rule is violated";
    }
}

I see that in your project the `Rule` interface, the `Position` class, and the `Empty` piece live in different packages than you assumed, and that `Move` does not have a `getTarget()` but a `getDestination()` method. Adjusting your imports and method names accordingly fixes the errors.

```java
package assignment.piece;

import assignment.game.Game;
import assignment.game.Move;
import assignment.rules.Rule;
import assignment.model.Empty;
import assignment.model.Position;
import assignment.piece.Archer;

/**
 * The rule of moving of Archer, which is similar to the moving rule of cannon in Chinese chess.
 *
 * @see <a href='https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xiangqi#Cannon'>Wikipedia</a>
 */
public class ArcherMoveRule implements Rule {
    @Override
    public boolean validate(Game game, Move move) {
        // only validate Archer moves; non-Archers are handled elsewhere
        if (!(game.getPiece(move.getSource()) instanceof Archer)) {
            return true;
        }

        Position from = move.getSource();
        Position to = move.getDestination();

        int dx = Integer.compare(to.getCol(), from.getCol());
        int dy = Integer.compare(to.getRow(), from.getRow());

        // must move strictly horizontally or vertically
        if (dx != 0 && dy != 0) {
            return false;
        }

        // count intervening pieces between from and to (exclusive)
        int screens = 0;
        Position curr = from.offset(dy, dx);
        while (!curr.equals(to)) {
            if (!(game.getPiece(curr) instanceof Empty)) {
                screens++;
            }
            curr = curr.offset(dy, dx);
        }

        boolean isCapture = !(game.getPiece(to) instanceof Empty);

        if (isCapture) {
            // capturing move: exactly one screen required
            return screens == 1;
        } else {
            // non-capture move: no screens allowed
            return screens == 0;
        }
    }

    @Override
    public String getDescription() {
        return "archer move rule is violated";
    }
}
```

**What was fixed:**
1. **Imports** – `Rule`, `Position`, `Empty`, `Game`, and `Move` were imported from their actual packages.
2. **Method name** – switched from `move.getTarget()` to `move.getDestination()`, which matches your `Move` API.
3. **Removed incorrect import of `assignment.protocol`** and replaced it with the correct packages.

With these changes, the class should compile under Java 19.

import assignment.protocol.Game;

import assignment.protocol.Rule;

/**
 * The rule of moving of Archer, which is similar to the moving rule of cannon in Chinese chess.
 *
```java
 * @see <a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xiangqi#Cannon">Wikipedia</a>
 */
public class ArcherMoveRule implements Rule {

    @Override
    public boolean validate(Game game, Move move) {

        Piece srcPiece = game.getPiece(move.getSource());

            return true;

        Position to   = move.getTarget();

        int dx = Integer.compare(to.getCol(), from.getCol());
        int dy = Integer.compare(to.getRow(), from.getRow());

        // must move strictly horizontally or vertically
        if (dx != 0 && dy != 0) {
            return false;
        }

        // count intervening pieces ("screens") between from and to (exclusive)
        int screens = 0;
        Position curr = from.offset(dy, dx);
        while (!curr.equals(to)) {
            if (!(game.getPiece(curr) instanceof assignment.protocol.Empty)) {
                screens++;
            }
            curr = curr.offset(dy, dx);
        }

        boolean isCapture = !(game.getPiece(to) instanceof assignment.protocol.Empty);
        // capture: exactly one screen; non‑capture: no screens
        return isCapture ? (screens == 1) : (screens == 0);
    }

    @Override
    public String getDescription() {
        return "archer move rule is violated";
    }
}
```

package assignment.piece;

import assignment.protocol.Game;
import assignment.protocol.Move;
import assignment.protocol.Rule;
import assignment.protocol.Piece;
import assignment.protocol.Position;

/**
 * The rule of moving of Archer, which is similar to the moving rule of cannon in Chinese chess.
 *
 * @see <a href='https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xiangqi#Cannon'>Wikipedia</a>
 */
public class ArcherMoveRule implements Rule {
    @Override
    public boolean validate(Game game, Move move) {
        // only validate Archer moves; non-Archers are handled elsewhere
        if (!(game.getPiece(move.getSource()) instanceof Archer)) {
            return true;
        }

        Position from = move.getSource();
        Position to = move.getTarget();

        int dx = Integer.compare(to.getCol(), from.getCol());
        int dy = Integer.compare(to.getRow(), from.getRow());

        // must move strictly horizontally or vertically
        if (dx != 0 && dy != 0) {
            return false;
        }

        // count intervening pieces between from and to (exclusive)
        int screens = 0;
        Position curr = from.offset(dy, dx);
        while (!curr.equals(to)) {
            if (!(game.getPiece(curr) instanceof Empty)) {
                screens++;
            }
            curr = curr.offset(dy, dx);
        }

        Piece targetPiece = game.getPiece(to);
        boolean isCapture = !(targetPiece instanceof Empty);

        if (isCapture) {
            // capturing move: exactly one screen required
            return screens == 1;
        } else {
            // non-capture move: no screens allowed
            return screens == 0;
        }
    }

    @Override
    public String getDescription() {
        return "archer move rule is violated";
    }
}

/**
 * The rule of moving of Archer, which is similar to the moving rule of cannon in Chinese chess.
 *
 * @see <a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xiangqi#Cannon">Wikipedia</a>
 */
public class ArcherMoveRule implements Rule {

    @Override
    public boolean validate(Game game, Move move) {
        // only validate Archer moves; non-Archers are handled elsewhere
        Piece srcPiece = game.getPiece(move.getSource());
        if (!(srcPiece instanceof Archer)) {
            return true;
        }

        Position from = move.getSource();
        Position to   = move.getTarget();

        int dx = Integer.compare(to.getCol(), from.getCol());
        int dy = Integer.compare(to.getRow(), from.getRow());

        // must move strictly horizontally or vertically
        if (dx != 0 && dy != 0) {
            return false;
        }

        // count intervening pieces ("screens") between from and to (exclusive)
        int screens = 0;
        Position curr = from.offset(dy, dx);
        while (!curr.equals(to)) {
            if (!(game.getPiece(curr) instanceof assignment.protocol.Empty)) {
                screens++;
            }
            curr = curr.offset(dy, dx);
        }

        boolean isCapture = !(game.getPiece(to) instanceof assignment.protocol.Empty);
        // capture: exactly one screen; non‑capture: no screens
        return isCapture ? (screens == 1) : (screens == 0);

Response Text:---
I’m going to implement the knight’s L‑shaped move test in `validate(…)`, i.e. exactly two squares in one direction and one in the other. We’ll compute the row‑ and column‑offsets between source and target and return true only if they form {2,1}. Here is the fully completed class (with the TODO removed).  

```java
package assignment.piece;

import assignment.protocol.Game;
import assignment.protocol.Move;

/**
 * Moving rule of Knight in chess (no block)
 */
public class KnightMoveRule implements Rule {

    @Override
    public boolean validate(Game game, Move move) {
        // only apply to Knights; other pieces aren’t our concern
        if (!(game.getPiece(move.getSource()) instanceof Knight)) {
            return true;
        }

        int fromRank = move.getSource().rank();
        int fromFile = move.getSource().file();
        int toRank   = move.getTarget().rank();
        int toFile   = move.getTarget().file();

        int rankDiff = Math.abs(toRank  - fromRank);
        int fileDiff = Math.abs(toFile  - fromFile);

        // must move in an L: one axis = 2, the other = 1
        return (rankDiff == 2 && fileDiff == 1)
            || (rankDiff == 1 && fileDiff == 2);
    }

    @Override
    public String getDescription() {
        return "knight move rule is violated";
    }
}
```
【F:assignment/piece/KnightMoveRule.java†L1-L27】

Explanation of the key change:

- **Compute deltas**: we extract ranks/files from source/target squares and take absolute differences.
- **L‑shape check**: we return true only if `(rankDiff, fileDiff)` is exactly `(2,1)` or `(1,2)`.
  
This satisfies the knight’s unique “no‑block” jump rule in chess.

Response Text:---
It turns out the protocol API doesn’t expose a `getTarget()` on `Move` nor `rank()/file()` on `Place`. Instead, `Move` defines `from()` and `to()` returning `Place`, and `Place` exposes `row()` and `column()`. Updating the code accordingly fixes the errors.

**KnightMoveRule.java**  
```java
package assignment.piece;

import assignment.protocol.Game;
import assignment.protocol.Move;

/**
 * Moving rule of Knight in chess (no block)
 */
public class KnightMoveRule implements Rule {

    @Override
    public boolean validate(Game game, Move move) {
        if (!(game.getPiece(move.from()) instanceof Knight)) {
            return true;
        }

        int fromRow    = move.from().row();
        int fromColumn = move.from().column();
        int toRow      = move.to().row();
        int toColumn   = move.to().column();

        int rowDiff    = Math.abs(toRow    - fromRow);
        int colDiff    = Math.abs(toColumn - fromColumn);

        // must move in an L: one axis = 2, the other = 1
        return (rowDiff == 2 && colDiff == 1)
            || (rowDiff == 1 && colDiff == 2);
    }

    @Override
    public String getDescription() {
        return "knight move rule is violated";
    }
}
```

Response Text:---
It looks like there is no public `Rule` interface in the repo but you already have in your snippet:

```java
package assignment.piece;

public interface Rule {
    boolean validate(Game game, Move move);
    String getDescription();
}
```

so we’ll just implement the `validate(...)` in `OutOfBoundaryRule` by checking that both source and destination coordinates lie within `[0, width)`×`[0, height)`. From the protocols (`assignment.protocol.Game` and `assignment.protocol.Move`) you’ll typically have methods like `getHeight()`, `getWidth()`, and in `Move` something like `getSrcRow()`, `getSrcColumn()`, `getDstRow()`, `getDstColumn()` (the actual names may vary slightly—just adapt them).

Below is a self‑contained, complete `OutOfBoundaryRule.java` with the TODO filled in (and the TODO comment removed). Adjust the getter names to match your real `Game`/`Move` APIs if needed.

```java
package assignment.piece;

import assignment.protocol.Game;
import assignment.protocol.Move;

/**
 * Global rule that requires the source and destination should be inside the board boundary.
 */
public class OutOfBoundaryRule implements Rule {
    @Override
    public boolean validate(Game game, Move move) {
        int width = game.getWidth();
        int height = game.getHeight();
        int srcRow = move.getSrcRow();
        int srcCol = move.getSrcColumn();
        int dstRow = move.getDstRow();
        int dstCol = move.getDstColumn();

        // Check source is in bounds
        boolean srcInBounds = srcRow >= 0 && srcRow < height
                           && srcCol >= 0 && srcCol < width;
        // Check destination is in bounds
        boolean dstInBounds = dstRow >= 0 && dstRow < height
                           && dstCol >= 0 && dstCol < width;

        return srcInBounds && dstInBounds;
    }

    @Override
    public String getDescription() {
        return "place is out of boundary of gameboard";
    }
}
```

**Explanation**  
We fetch the board dimensions from the `Game` (`getWidth()`/`getHeight()`) and the source/destination coordinates from the `Move`. Then we simply ensure each coordinate lies within `0 ≤ row < height` and `0 ≤ column < width`. If both source and destination satisfy these bounds, `validate()` returns `true`; otherwise it returns `false`.

Response Text:---
It looks like your piece‐classes (Archer, Knight, ConsolePlayer, etc.) refer to `OutOfBoundaryRule` without importing it. To fix the “cannot be resolved to a type” errors you need to add the proper import in each of those classes.

Below is one example—update your **Archer.java** (and similarly for Knight, ConsolePlayer, etc.) by importing the rule:

```java
package assignment.piece;

import assignment.protocol.Game;
import assignment.protocol.Move;
import assignment.piece.OutOfBoundaryRule;  // <-- add this import

/**
 * Archer piece implementation.
 */
public class Archer implements Piece {
    // … your existing fields …

    @Override
    public boolean validateMove(Game game, Move move) {
        // apply out‑of‑boundary check first
        if (!new OutOfBoundaryRule().validate(game, move)) {
            return false;
        }
        // … rest of your validation logic …
    }

    // … other methods …
}
```

**Brief Explanation:**  
Every class that mentions `OutOfBoundaryRule` must import it from its package (`assignment.piece`). Adding the import eliminates the “cannot be resolved to a type” compilation errors. Make sure you repeat the same import line in **Knight.java**, **ConsolePlayer.java**, and any other class that uses `OutOfBoundaryRule`.

Response Text:---
I’m assuming you already have other piece‑implementations in the codebase that follow a similar pattern: scan in each of the four orthogonal directions, build candidate Move objects, run them through validateMove(…) (which applies your chain of Rules), and collect the ones that pass.

Below is a single, self‑contained Java class for `Archer` that completes the TODO in `getAvailableMoves`. It generates all straight‑line moves (up/down/left/right) both for non‑capture “riding” moves and for capture moves “jumping” exactly one intervening piece (the Xiangqi cannon rule). It then filters them through your existing `validateMove(...)` pipeline.

```java
package assignment.piece;

import assignment.protocol.Game;
import assignment.protocol.Move;
import assignment.protocol.Piece;
import assignment.protocol.Place;
import assignment.protocol.Player;

import java.util.ArrayList;
import java.util.List;

/**
 * Archer piece that moves similar to cannon in Chinese chess.
 * Rules of move of Archer can be found in Wikipedia
 * (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xiangqi#Cannon).
 *
 * @see <a href='https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xiangqi#Cannon'>Wikipedia</a>
 */
public class Archer extends Piece {
    public Archer(Player player) {
        super(player);
    }

    @Override
    public char getLabel() {
        return 'A';
    }

    /**
     * Returns an array of moves that are valid given the current place of the piece.
     * Generates all orthogonal moves: either “riding” any number of empty squares,
     * or “jumping” over exactly one intervening piece to capture an enemy.
     *
     * @param game   the game object
     * @param source the current place of this Archer
     * @return an array of available moves
     */
    @Override
    public Move[] getAvailableMoves(Game game, Place source) {
        List<Move> moves = new ArrayList<>();

        // four orthogonal directions: (dx, dy)
        int[][] deltas = { {1, 0}, {-1, 0}, {0, 1}, {0, -1} };
        for (int[] d : deltas) {
            int dx = d[0], dy = d[1];
            Place cursor = source.step(dx, dy);

            // first, any number of vacant steps (non-captures)
            while (cursor != null && game.getPieceAt(cursor) == null) {
                Move m = new Move(source, cursor);
                if (validateMove(game, m)) {
                    moves.add(m);
                }
                cursor = cursor.step(dx, dy);
            }

            // then, if we stopped at a piece, skip exactly one piece
            if (cursor != null && game.getPieceAt(cursor) != null) {
                // skip this intervening piece
                cursor = cursor.step(dx, dy);
                // then look for a single capture square
                if (cursor != null && game.getPieceAt(cursor) != null) {
                    Move m = new Move(source, cursor);
                    if (validateMove(game, m)) {
                        moves.add(m);
                    }
                }
            }
        }

        return moves.toArray(Move[]::new);
    }

    private boolean validateMove(Game game, Move move) {
        var rules = new Rule[] {
            new OutOfBoundaryRule(),
            new OccupiedRule(),
            new VacantRule(),
            new NilMoveRule(),
            new FirstNMovesProtectionRule(game.getConfiguration().getNumMovesProtection()),
            new ArcherMoveRule(),
        };
        for (var rule : rules) {
            if (!rule.validate(game, move)) {
                return false;
            }
        }
        return true;
    }
}
```

**Explanation (brief):**  
1. We iterate in each of the four straight directions.  
2. First we “ride” through empty squares, collecting non‑capture moves until we hit a piece or board edge.  
3. If we first encountered a piece, we step one more square beyond it; if that next square also holds a piece (enemy), we generate exactly one capture move over the intervening piece.  
4. Finally, every generated move is run through `validateMove(...)` to enforce boundary, occupancy, protection, and your custom `ArcherMoveRule`.  

This completes the TODO and matches the cannon‐style move rules.

     * Returns an array of moves that are valid given the current place of the piece.
     * Generates all orthogonal moves: either “riding” any number of empty squares,
     * or “jumping” over exactly one intervening piece to capture an enemy.
     *
     * @param game   the game object
     * @param source the current place of this Archer
     * @return an array of available moves
     */
    @Override
    public Move[] getAvailableMoves(Game game, Place source) {
        List<Move> moves = new ArrayList<>();

        // four orthogonal directions: (dx, dy)
        int[][] deltas = { {1, 0}, {-1, 0}, {0, 1}, {0, -1} };
        for (int[] d : deltas) {
            int dx = d[0], dy = d[1];
            Place cursor = source.step(dx, dy);

            // first, any number of vacant steps (non-captures)
            while (cursor != null && game.getPieceAt(cursor) == null) {
                Move m = new Move(source, cursor);
                if (validateMove(game, m)) {
                    moves.add(m);
                }
                cursor = cursor.step(dx, dy);
            }

            // then, if we stopped at a piece, skip exactly one piece
            if (cursor != null && game.getPieceAt(cursor) != null) {
                // skip this intervening piece
                cursor = cursor.step(dx, dy);
                // then look for a single capture square
                if (cursor != null && game.getPieceAt(cursor) != null) {
                    Move m = new Move(source, cursor);
                    if (validateMove(game, m)) {
                        moves.add(m);
                    }
                }
            }
        }

        return moves.toArray(Move[]::new);
    }

    private boolean validateMove(Game game, Move move) {
        var rules = new Rule[] {
            new OutOfBoundaryRule(),
            new OccupiedRule(),
            new VacantRule(),
            new NilMoveRule(),
            new FirstNMovesProtectionRule(game.getConfiguration().getNumMovesProtection()),
            new ArcherMoveRule(),
        };
        for (var rule : rules) {
            if (!rule.validate(game, move)) {
                return false;
            }
        }
        return true;
    }

package assignment.piece;

import assignment.protocol.Game;
import assignment.protocol.Move;
import assignment.protocol.Piece;
import assignment.protocol.Place;
import assignment.protocol.Player;

import java.util.ArrayList;
import java.util.List;

/**
 * Archer piece that moves similar to cannon in Chinese chess.
 * Rules of move of Archer can be found in Wikipedia
 * (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xiangqi#Cannon).
 *
 * @see <a href='https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xiangqi#Cannon'>Wikipedia</a>
 */
public class Archer extends Piece {
    public Archer(Player player) {
        super(player);
    }

    @Override
    public char getLabel() {
        return 'A';
    }

    /**
     * Returns an array of moves that are valid given the current place of the piece.
     * Generates all orthogonal moves: either “riding” any number of empty squares,
     * or “jumping” over exactly one intervening piece to capture an enemy.
     *
     * @param game   the game object
     * @param source the current place of this Archer
     * @return an array of available moves
     */
    @Override
    public Move[] getAvailableMoves(Game game, Place source) {
        List<Move> moves = new ArrayList<>();

        // four orthogonal directions: (dx, dy)
        int[][] deltas = { {1, 0}, {-1, 0}, {0, 1}, {0, -1} };
        for (int[] d : deltas) {
            int dx = d[0], dy = d[1];
            Place cursor = source.step(dx, dy);

            // first, any number of vacant steps (non-captures)
            while (cursor != null && game.getPieceAt(cursor) == null) {
                Move m = new Move(source, cursor);
                if (validateMove(game, m)) {
                    moves.add(m);
                }
                cursor = cursor.step(dx, dy);
            }

            // then, if we stopped at a piece, skip exactly one piece
            if (cursor != null && game.getPieceAt(cursor) != null) {
                // skip this intervening piece
                cursor = cursor.step(dx, dy);
                // then look for a single capture square
                if (cursor != null && game.getPieceAt(cursor) != null) {
                    Move m = new Move(source, cursor);
                    if (validateMove(game, m)) {
                        moves.add(m);
                    }
                }
            }
        }

        return moves.toArray(Move[]::new);
    }

    private boolean validateMove(Game game, Move move) {
        var rules = new Rule[] {
            new OutOfBoundaryRule(),
            new OccupiedRule(),
            new VacantRule(),
            new NilMoveRule(),
            new FirstNMovesProtectionRule(game.getConfiguration().getNumMovesProtection()),
            new ArcherMoveRule(),
        };
        for (var rule : rules) {
            if (!rule.validate(game, move)) {
                return false;
            }
        }
        return true;
    }
}

import assignment.protocol.Game;
import assignment.protocol.Move;
import assignment.protocol.Piece;
import assignment.protocol.Place;
import assignment.protocol.Player;

import java.util.ArrayList;
import java.util.List;

/**
 * Archer piece that moves similar to cannon in Chinese chess.
 * Rules of move of Archer can be found in Wikipedia
 * (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xiangqi#Cannon).
 *
 * @see <a href='https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xiangqi#Cannon'>Wikipedia</a>
 */
public class Archer extends Piece {
    public Archer(Player player) {
        super(player);
    }

    @Override
    public char getLabel() {
        return 'A';
    }

    /**
     * Returns an array of moves that are valid given the current place of the piece.
     * Generates all orthogonal moves: either “riding” any number of empty squares,
     * or “jumping” over exactly one intervening piece to capture an enemy.
     *
     * @param game   the game object
     * @param source the current place of this Archer
     * @return an array of available moves
     */
    @Override
    public Move[] getAvailableMoves(Game game, Place source) {
        List<Move> moves = new ArrayList<>();

```java
        // four orthogonal directions: (drow, dcol)
        int[][] deltas = { {1, 0}, {-1, 0}, {0, 1}, {0, -1} };
        for (int[] delta : deltas) {
            int drow = delta[0], dcol = delta[1];
            Place cursor = source.moveBy(drow, dcol);

            // first, any number of vacant steps (non-captures)
            while (cursor != null && game.getPiece(cursor) == null) {
                Move m = new Move(source, cursor);
                if (validateMove(game, m)) {
                    moves.add(m);
                }
                cursor = cursor.moveBy(drow, dcol);
            }

            // then, if we stopped at a piece, skip exactly one piece
            if (cursor != null && game.getPiece(cursor) != null) {
                // skip this intervening piece
                cursor = cursor.moveBy(drow, dcol);
                // then look for a single capture square
                if (cursor != null && game.getPiece(cursor) != null) {
                    Move m = new Move(source, cursor);
                    if (validateMove(game, m)) {
                        moves.add(m);
                    }
                }
            }
        }

        return moves.toArray(Move[]::new);
    }

    private boolean validateMove(Game game, Move move) {
        var rules = new Rule[] {
            new OutOfBoundaryRule(),
            new OccupiedRule(),
            new VacantRule(),
            new NilMoveRule(),
            new FirstNMovesProtectionRule(game.getConfiguration().getNumMovesProtection()),
            new ArcherMoveRule(),
        };
        for (var rule : rules) {
            if (!rule.validate(game, move)) {
                return false;
            }
        }
        return true;
    }
}
```

```java
package assignment.piece;

import assignment.protocol.Game;
import assignment.protocol.Move;
import assignment.protocol.Piece;
import assignment.protocol.Place;
import assignment.protocol.Player;

import java.util.ArrayList;
import java.util.List;

/**
 * Archer piece that moves similar to cannon in Chinese chess.
 * Rules of move of Archer can be found in Wikipedia
 * (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xiangqi#Cannon).
 *
 * @see <a href='https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xiangqi#Cannon'>Wikipedia</a>
 */
public class Archer extends Piece {
    public Archer(Player player) {
        super(player);
    }

    @Override
    public char getLabel() {
        return 'A';
    }

    /**
     * Returns an array of moves that are valid given the current place of the piece.
     * Generates all orthogonal moves: either “riding” any number of empty squares,
     * or “jumping” over exactly one intervening piece to capture an enemy.
     *
     * @param game   the game object
     * @param source the current place of this Archer
     * @return an array of available moves
     */
    @Override
    public Move[] getAvailableMoves(Game game, Place source) {
        List<Move> moves = new ArrayList<>();

        // Four orthogonal directions: (dRow, dCol)
        int[][] deltas = { {1, 0}, {-1, 0}, {0, 1}, {0, -1} };
        for (int[] delta : deltas) {
            int dRow = delta[0], dCol = delta[1];
            // advance one step in this direction
            Place cursor = Place.of(source.row() + dRow, source.column() + dCol);

            // ride over empty squares
            while (cursor != null && game.getPieceAt(cursor) == null) {
                Move m = new Move(source, cursor);
                if (validateMove(game, m)) {
                    moves.add(m);
                }
                cursor = Place.of(cursor.row() + dRow, cursor.column() + dCol);
            }

            // if we hit a piece, skip exactly one, then try a capture
            if (cursor != null && game.getPieceAt(cursor) != null) {
                // skip the intervening piece
                cursor = Place.of(cursor.row() + dRow, cursor.column() + dCol);
                // attempt capture (must land on another piece)
                if (cursor != null && game.getPieceAt(cursor) != null) {
                    Move m = new Move(source, cursor);
                    if (validateMove(game, m)) {
                        moves.add(m);
                    }
                }
            }
        }

        return moves.toArray(Move[]::new);
    }

    private boolean validateMove(Game game, Move move) {
        var rules = new Rule[] {
            new OutOfBoundaryRule(),
            new OccupiedRule(),
            new VacantRule(),
            new NilMoveRule(),
            new FirstNMovesProtectionRule(game.getConfiguration().getNumMovesProtection()),
            new ArcherMoveRule(),
        };
        for (var rule : rules) {
            if (!rule.validate(game, move)) {
                return false;
            }
        }
        return true;
    }
}
```

I’ll adjust the implementation to match the actual Move API instead of calling the non‑existent getFrom()/getTo(). In our protocol, a Move object exposes source and destination squares via getSrcX()/getSrcY() and getDstX()/getDstY(). **NilMoveRule.java**  
```java
package assignment.piece;

import assignment.protocol.Game;
import assignment.protocol.Move;

/**
 * Global rule that requires the source and destination of a move should not be the same.
 */
public class NilMoveRule implements Rule {

    @Override
    public boolean validate(Game game, Move move) {
        // source and destination must differ in at least one coordinate
        return move.getSrcX() != move.getDstX()
            || move.getSrcY() != move.getDstY();
    }

    @Override
    public String getDescription() {
        return "the source and destination of move should be different places";
    }
}
```

I’ll implement `getAvailableMoves(...)` by generating all eight “L‑shaped” offsets for a knight, building a `Move` for each, and then filtering them through `validateMove(...)`. Below is the completed `Knight.java` with the TODO removed and replaced by the concrete logic.

```java
package assignment.piece;

import assignment.protocol.Game;
import assignment.protocol.Move;
import assignment.protocol.Piece;
import assignment.protocol.Place;
import assignment.protocol.Player;

import java.util.ArrayList;
import java.util.List;

/**
 * Knight piece that moves similar to knight in chess.
 * Rules of move of Knight can be found in wikipedia (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Knight_(chess)).
 *
 * @see <a href='https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Knight_(chess)'>Wikipedia</a>
 */
public class Knight extends Piece {
    public Knight(Player player) {
        super(player);
    }

    @Override
    public char getLabel() {
        return 'K';
    }

    /**
     * Returns an array of moves that are valid given the current place of the piece.
     * Given the {@link Game} object and the {@link Place} that current knight piece locates, this method should
     * return ALL VALID {@link Move}s according to the current {@link Place} of this knight piece.
     * All the returned {@link Move} should have source equal to the source parameter.
     * <p>
     * Hint: you should consider corner cases when the {@link Move} is not valid on the gameboard.
     * Several tests are provided and your implementation should pass them.
     * <p>
     * <strong>Attention: Student should make sure all {@link Move}s returned are valid.</strong>
     *
     * @param game   the game object
     * @param source the current place of the piece
     * @return an array of available moves
     */
    @Override
    public Move[] getAvailableMoves(Game game, Place source) {
        // All eight possible "L-shaped" knight moves
        int[][] deltas = {
            {  2,  1 }, {  2, -1 }, { -2,  1 }, { -2, -1 },
            {  1,  2 }, {  1, -2 }, { -1,  2 }, { -1, -2 }
        };

        List<Move> candidates = new ArrayList<>();
        for (int[] d : deltas) {
            int newRow = source.row() + d[0];
            int newCol = source.col() + d[1];
            Move m = new Move(source, Place.of(newRow, newCol));
            if (validateMove(game, m)) {
                candidates.add(m);
            }
        }
        return candidates.toArray(Move[]::new);
    }

    private boolean validateMove(Game game, Move move) {
        var rules = new Rule[] {
            new OutOfBoundaryRule(),
            new OccupiedRule(),
            new VacantRule(),
            new NilMoveRule(),
            new FirstNMovesProtectionRule(game.getConfiguration().getNumMovesProtection()),
            new KnightMoveRule(),
            new KnightBlockRule(),
        };
        for (var rule : rules) {
            if (!rule.validate(game, move)) {
                return false;
            }
        }
        return true;
    }
}
```

package assignment.piece;

import assignment.protocol.Game;
import assignment.protocol.Move;
import assignment.protocol.Piece;
import assignment.protocol.Place;
import assignment.protocol.Player;

import java.util.ArrayList;
import java.util.List;

/**
 * Knight piece that moves similar to knight in chess.
 * Rules of move of Knight can be found in wikipedia (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Knight_(chess)).
 *
 * @see <a href='https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Knight_(chess)'>Wikipedia</a>
 */
public class Knight extends Piece {
    public Knight(Player player) {
        super(player);
    }

    @Override
    public char getLabel() {
        return 'K';
    }

    /**
     * Returns an array of moves that are valid given the current place of the piece.
     * Given the {@link Game} object and the {@link Place} that current knight piece locates, this method should
     * return ALL VALID {@link Move}s according to the current {@link Place} of this knight piece.
     * All the returned {@link Move} should have source equal to the source parameter.
     * <p>
     * Hint: you should consider corner cases when the {@link Move} is not valid on the gameboard.
     * Several tests are provided and your implementation should pass them.
     * <p>
     * <strong>Attention: Student should make sure all {@link Move}s returned are valid.</strong>
     *
     * @param game   the game object
     * @param source the current place of the piece
     * @return an array of available moves
     */
    @Override
    public Move[] getAvailableMoves(Game game, Place source) {
        // All eight possible "L-shaped" knight moves
        int[][] deltas = {
            {  2,  1 }, {  2, -1 }, { -2,  1 }, { -2, -1 },
            {  1,  2 }, {  1, -2 }, { -1,  2 }, { -1, -2 }
        };

        List<Move> candidates = new ArrayList<>();
        for (int[] d : deltas) {
            int newRow = source.row() + d[0];
            int newCol = source.col() + d[1];
            Move m = new Move(source, Place.of(newRow, newCol));
            if (validateMove(game, m)) {
                candidates.add(m);
            }
        }
        return candidates.toArray(Move[]::new);
    }

    private boolean validateMove(Game game, Move move) {
        var rules = new Rule[] {
            new OutOfBoundaryRule(),
            new OccupiedRule(),
            new VacantRule(),
            new NilMoveRule(),
            new FirstNMovesProtectionRule(game.getConfiguration().getNumMovesProtection()),
            new KnightMoveRule(),
            new KnightBlockRule(),
        };
        for (var rule : rules) {
            if (!rule.validate(game, move)) {
                return false;
            }
        }
        return true;
    }
}

 * Rules of move of Knight can be found in wikipedia (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Knight_(chess)).
 *
 * @see <a href='https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Knight_(chess)'>Wikipedia</a>
 */
public class Knight extends Piece {
    public Knight(Player player) {
        super(player);
    }

    @Override
    public char getLabel() {
        return 'K';
    }

    /**
     * Returns an array of moves that are valid given the current place of the piece.
     * Given the {@link Game} object and the {@link Place} that current knight piece locates, this method should
     * return ALL VALID {@link Move}s according to the current {@link Place} of this knight piece.
     * All the returned {@link Move} should have source equal to the source parameter.
     * <p>
     * Hint: you should consider corner cases when the {@link Move} is not valid on the gameboard.
     * Several tests are provided and your implementation should pass them.
     * <p>
     * <strong>Attention: Student should make sure all {@link Move}s returned are valid.</strong>
     *
     * @param game   the game object
     * @param source the current place of the piece
     * @return an array of available moves
     */
    @Override
    public Move[] getAvailableMoves(Game game, Place source) {
        // All eight possible "L-shaped" knight moves
        int[][] deltas = {
            {  2,  1 }, {  2, -1 }, { -2,  1 }, { -2, -1 },
            {  1,  2 }, {  1, -2 }, { -1,  2 }, { -1, -2 }
        };

        List<Move> candidates = new ArrayList<>();
        for (int[] d : deltas) {
```java
            int newRow = source.getRow() + d[0];
            int newCol = source.getColumn() + d[1];
            Place target = new Place(newRow, newCol);
            Move m = new Move(source, target);
            if (validateMove(game, m)) {
                candidates.add(m);
            }
        }

        return candidates.toArray(Move[]::new);
    }

    private boolean validateMove(Game game, Move move) {
        var rules = new Rule[] {
            new OutOfBoundaryRule(),
            new OccupiedRule(),
            new VacantRule(),
            new NilMoveRule(),
            new FirstNMovesProtectionRule(game.getConfiguration().getNumMovesProtection()),
            new KnightMoveRule(),
            new KnightBlockRule(),
        };
        for (var rule : rules) {
            if (!rule.validate(game, move)) {
                return false;
            }
        }
        return true;
    }
}
```

Response Text:---
**Explanation**

The `OccupiedRule` must forbid moves whose target square is already occupied by one of the moving player’s own pieces. To implement this, we ask the game for the piece at the destination position (`move.getTo()`); if it’s non‑null and its owner matches the moving piece’s owner, the rule fails.

---

```java
package assignment.piece;

import assignment.protocol.Game;
import assignment.protocol.Move;
import assignment.protocol.Piece;
import assignment.protocol.Player;

/**
 * Global rule that requires that a piece should not go to a destination where there is another piece belonging to the
 * same player.
 */
public class OccupiedRule implements Rule {
    @Override
    public boolean validate(Game game, Move move) {
        // get the piece that is about to move and the piece (if any) at the destination
        Piece movingPiece   = game.getPieceAt(move.getFrom());
        Piece targetPiece   = game.getPieceAt(move.getTo());
        Player movingPlayer = movingPiece.getOwner();

        // invalid if there's a piece owned by the same player at the destination
        return targetPiece == null || !targetPiece.getOwner().equals(movingPlayer);
    }

    @Override
    public String getDescription() {
        return "piece cannot be captured by another piece belonging to the same player";
    }
}
```

**Notes**
- We retrieve both the moving piece and any piece already on the destination square.
- The move is valid only if the target square is empty or occupied by an opponent’s piece.
